config.providers.description: LLM services that speak the OpenAI chat API. Each entry has a unique `name`, a `baseUrl`, the API root such as `http://localhost:11434/v1`, and an optional `caFile` for a corporate or self-signed certificate. API keys are stored in the editor's secret storage, never here. Read from user settings only: a workspace cannot override this list, so a repository cannot redirect a stored key.
config.providers.name.description: Unique name shown in the chat panel.
config.providers.baseUrl.description: API root, for example `http://localhost:11434/v1`. broke-code appends `/models` and `/chat/completions`.
config.providers.caFile.description: Optional PEM file of extra certificate authorities to trust for this provider only, such as a corporate or self-signed CA. Absolute path, or starting with `~/`. It adds to the system certificates, never replaces them. Certificate verification cannot be turned off.
config.contextSizes.description: Context size of each model, in tokens, by model name as the provider lists it, for example `{ "gemma-4": 262144, "qwen3:8b": 40960 }`. A model absent from this table, or with a size that is not a positive whole number, uses 32,768. An agent turn stops before a request whose estimated size (characters divided by the characters per token learned from the replies, 4 at first) leaves less than one eighth of the context for the reply, even with older tool results left out, unless `brokeCode.autoCompact` summarizes the conversation first. Read from user settings only.
config.maxToolSteps.description: Tool steps an agent turn may take before it stops: tool calls and malformed calls alike. At least 1. A turn in flight keeps the limit it started with. Read from user settings only.
config.autoCompact.description: When an agent turn's next request would not fit the model's context, even with older tool results left out, ask the model for a summary of the conversation, as `/compact` does, and go on with the turn instead of stopping it. The request then sends the summary and the turn's message in place of everything before them. At most one summary per request. Off by default, since it adds a request you did not ask for. A turn reads it when it starts. Read from user settings only.
config.autoApproveWrites.description: Apply the agent's file changes (`write_file`, `edit_file`) without asking: no diff opens and no Accept is needed; the chat marks each such step as auto-approved. Off by default. Commands always ask, whatever this says. A file with unsaved changes in an editor is never written. Read from user settings only: a workspace cannot turn approval off. The mode selector in the chat's message box shows this setting and writes it: Auto-edit is on, Ask is off. As a user setting, it applies to every window. Its third mode, Plan, kept per workspace, gives the agent the read tools only and leaves this setting as it is.
config.commandTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a command the agent runs (`run_command`) may take before its process group is stopped: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL two seconds later. A process that left the group (setsid, a daemon) is not stopped. The model gets the output so far. At least 1. Read at each command, from user settings only: a workspace cannot change it.
config.notifications.description: Show a notification when an agent turn or `/compact` ends, fails, or stops on a limit, or when a file change or a command waits for your decision, while the chat is not in view: the chat view is hidden, or the window does not have the focus. Each notification has a Show chat button. A turn you stop shows none. On by default. Read at each event, from user settings only: only the user value `false` turns the notifications off.
